method: One separate agent for each run. 3 runs for each variant. Use the prompt in runner.md.
Variants: baseline (same request, no skill) and skill (the skill of the case, from plugins/dev-stack/skills/<skill>).
Each run works on its own copy of the fixture in <run>/repo. Sub-agents are not available in a run.
Assertions are yes or no. A 'check' assertion is scored by score.py. A 'judge' assertion is scored by one grader agent for each run (grader.md). The grader does not see the variant name.
human 'absent' means that nobody answers questions. The agent decides, and states each assumption and each open team decision in its final message.
A review case has an answer sheet in planted/<fixture>.json. Only the grader reads it. The run agent never sees it.

Standing rules of the human for all cases: MediatR and AutoMapper are not allowed. Each new package needs the approval of the human. For new code, an open team decision is asked (or, with human 'absent', marked as assumed), unless docs/dev-team/decisions.md has an accepted answer.

A trap case (name ends in '-trap') tests facts that a model trained before mid-2026 often gets wrong. The 'traps' field lists them, and each trap has its own assertion (field 'trap'). selftest.py proves each check on a wrong and a correct solution.

evals.name: postgresql-trap
evals.request: Warehouse workers pick orders. Add POST /picking/next. The worker sends its id in the header X-Worker-Id (text, at most 32 characters). The endpoint gives the worker the oldest placed order that no other worker has: it sets the status to Picking, stores the worker id and the start time, and returns 200 with the order in the same JSON shape as POST /orders. When no order is free, it returns 204. Twenty workers call it at the same time. A worker must never wait for another worker, and must never get an order that another worker has. Also add GET /reports/daily-sales?from=2026-07-01&to=2026-07-31. It returns one row per day in Amsterdam time, with the number of orders and the revenue (the sum of the line totals) of the orders that are not cancelled, as a JSON array: [{"day": "2026-07-02", "orders": 3, "revenue": 12.50}]. The orders table is big and gets writes all day. Add the EF Core migration.
traps: A read with LINQ, then an update, without a row lock: two workers get the same order. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED outside a transaction has the same result, because the lock ends with the statement.
Raw SQL with unquoted PascalCase names (WHERE Status = 'Placed') fails with 42703: the fixture has no snake_case convention.

SqlQuery over 'UPDATE ... RETURNING' composed with SingleOrDefaultAsync: EF wraps the SQL in a subquery and PostgreSQL rejects it. FromSql with 'SELECT *' on an entity with an xmin token fails with 42703.
SERIALIZABLE or REPEATABLE READ without a retry: 40001 under load.
Days in the session time zone (UTC), not in Amsterdam time: an order at 22:30Z on 2026-07-01 belongs to 2026-07-02.
A plain CREATE INDEX on the big live table blocks writes (DATA-25).

assertions.trap: Snapshot matches the model (has-pending-model-changes).
Double claim, unquoted names, composed RETURNING, 40001 without retry, UTC days.

assertions.judge: The claim is atomic and never waits: a row lock with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED inside one UPDATE statement or inside one explicit transaction, or an equivalent atomic conditional UPDATE. It does not use SERIALIZABLE or REPEATABLE READ without a retry, and it does not use a lock that makes a worker wait for another worker (FOR UPDATE without SKIP LOCKED, an advisory lock, a C# lock).

The daily report groups by the calendar day in Europe/Amsterdam (AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Amsterdam' in SQL, or TimeZoneInfo in code), and filters on the bare PlacedAt column with the UTC bounds of the local days (no function or cast on the column in the WHERE clause).

The migration adds an index for the claim query (a partial index on placed orders, or an index that starts with the status, with PlacedAt), and the index is built without blocking writes (IsCreatedConcurrently, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, or a separate step for the DBA). The final message names DDL on live tables (DATA-25) as an assumed decision or explains the lock risk.
The final message states the assumptions with the chosen answers: at least the time zone name, the status value for picking, and how the migration is deployed or how the index is built.

Use PuppeteerSharp (approved: PuppeteerSharp 25.14.0). It must run in our Docker image: change the Dockerfile too. In CI the browser path is in the environment variable PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH. Expect about 20 invoices per minute at peak.
traps: The customer note is free text from the webshop. Put into the HTML as markup, it makes Chrome request internal URLs (, ,
The remote logo conflicts with a blocked network. Inline it as a data URI or an embedded resource, or allow only its host.

As root, Chrome refuses to start with the sandbox on, so a model adds --no-sandbox or PUPPETEER_DANGEROUS_NO_SANDBOX. The fix is a non-root user in the image (USER $APP_UID), not a sandbox opt-out (SEC-24).

BrowserFetcher.DownloadAsync at startup downloads Chrome at runtime. Install chrome-headless-shell 155.0.8059.79 at image build time. Puppeteer.LaunchAsync in each request costs 1 to 2 seconds and a new process tree: use one browser per process and a concurrency limit.
A chiseled image cannot hold Chrome (OPS-03). Chrome needs system libraries, fonts, and an init process to reap its child processes.

assertions.trap: Customer note as markup: the renderer requests internal URLs (SSRF).
Customer note rendered as HTML, not as text.
Sandbox opt-out instead of a non-root user (SEC-24).
The image runs Chrome as root.
Runtime download of Chrome, or a browser for each request.

assertions.judge: The logo needs no network at render time: it is inlined as a data URI or an embedded resource, or only its host is allowed while every other URL is blocked. The final message explains the choice.

The renderer keeps one browser per process (a singleton that starts again after a disconnect and closes at shutdown), uses one context and one page per render with await using, limits concurrent pages, sets timeouts on SetContentAsync and PdfDataAsync, and blocks the network of the page.

The Dockerfile installs chrome-headless-shell 155.0.8059.79 (or the build of the PuppeteerSharp version) at build time, installs fonts (for example fonts-liberation) and an init process (tini, or documents docker run --init), stays on the full aspnet:10.0 image for the renderer, and runs as a non-root user.

The final message marks the open team decisions as assumed: at least the sandbox policy (SEC-24) or the base image of the renderer (OPS-03), and says how the customer note is treated (untrusted text, encoded, no network).
